headline: CBA's APRA Level 2 CET1 ratio rose 150 bpts to 13.1% in FY21 (from 11.6% in FY20), well above APRA's 10.5% 'unquestionably strong' benchmark. The improvement was driven by $8.7 billion of cash NPAT (+185 bpts total across both halves), divestment proceeds (+42 bpts from BoCommLife, CommInsure Life and other sales), and an APRA-operational-risk-add-on reduction (+17 bpts per APRA's Nov 2020 announcement cutting the add-on 50% from $12.5 bn to $6.25 bn), partly offset by dividends paid (-91 bpts; 2020 final DRP issued shares while 2021 interim DRP was fully on-market purchased at $418 m / 9 bpts impact), and net RWA movement (-5 bpts; credit RWA up $7.4 bn on volume growth, offset by $11.0 bn OpRisk RWA decline). The internationally comparable CET1 ratio rose 200 bpts to 19.4%.

drivers.narrative: Cash NPAT from continuing operations was $8,653 million, up 19.8% on FY20 ($7,225 million). Retail Banking Services contributed 95 bpts ($4,246 m organic capital), Business Banking 45 bpts ($2,060 m), ASB 20 bpts ($893 m), New Zealand 19 bpts ($847 m), offset by Corporate Centre consumption of 112 bpts ($5,044 m, largely dividends). LIE fell $1,964 million reflecting improved economic outlook.

Proceeds from sales of BoCommLife, CommInsure Life and other divestments since 1H19. Total divestment capital uplift of $7.9 billion, of which $6.2 billion was excess over the 10.5% benchmark. CommInsure Life sale added +2 bpts (final proceeds received in 1H21).

APRA's 20 November 2020 announcement resulted in a 50% reduction in CBA's operational RWA add-on, from $12.5 billion to $6.25 billion. This reduced OpRisk RWA by $7.3 billion (26%) in Retail Banking and contributed +17 bpts to CET1.

2020 final dividend: DRP satisfied by issuance of $264 million shares (15.2% participation), partially offsetting the dividend drag. 2021 interim dividend: DRP neutralised by on-market purchase of $418 million shares (15.7% participation, 9 bpts CET1 impact). Full year dividend $3.50/share (71% payout of cash NPAT).

Total RWA decreased $4.3 billion (1%) to $450.7 billion. Credit RWA increased $7.4 billion (2%) on volume growth in residential mortgages and commercial portfolios, partly offset by quality improvements. Traded Market Risk RWA fell $4.2 billion (34%). IRRBB RWA increased $3.5 billion (32%). OpRisk RWA fell $11.0 billion (19%), mainly from the APRA add-on reduction.

Net other regulatory adjustments: -2 bpts in 2H20 and +4 bpts in 1H21. Includes CommInsure Life sale proceeds (+2 bpts in 1H21) and equity accounted profits from associates (capital neutral per footnote).

limitations: Full-year RWA decomposition by sub-type (credit/market/operational/IRRBB) is derived from segment-level RWA tables rather than a dedicated full-year RWA bridge chart; individual sub-type bpts contributions are not separately stated by the bank for the full year.
The 'Other' bars (-2 bpts in 2H20, +4 bpts in 1H21) are not further decomposed by the bank beyond noting CommInsure Life proceeds (+2 bpts) and equity accounting neutrality.

The results presentation chart (p111) is the sole source for the full-year CET1 walk; the profit announcement (p53) only discloses half-on-half drivers (+97 bpts NPAT, +8 bpts RWA, +4 bpts other, -59 bpts dividend for 1H21).
The internationally comparable CET1 ratio (+200 bpts to 19.4%) is a different measure from APRA Level 2 and is reported as context only.
